title: “How the hell could you be so wrong?” AI agent leaked company founder’s personal bank accounts and expenses into work Slack
key_facts: IT founder and investor Shane Mack says his AI agent posted his personal bank balances and detailed expenses to his company's executive team Slack channel.
He says it posted a "monthly financial audit" on his behalf, including costs of a home gym project such as a septic tank, and credit card payments.
When he challenged Grok Bot, it replied that it was checking the channel and would delete the message.
Mack says it was his own mistake: he gave one bot access to his bank accounts, not realising it could exchange data with another bot managing the company's Slack.
He has turned off everything personal for now.
The post drew over 800,000 views; some users doubt it because Mack is building a tool to set permissions between AI assistants, which he denies is a stunt.
quote_evidence: As the investor later admitted, it was his own mistake.
Shane Mack himself denies the accusations of forgery and claims that the story is 100% real.
why_it_matters_hint: Linked AI assistants with broad access can pass private data to places the owner never meant.
event_date: Mack dates it to 'last Thursday' in his post; exact date not stated.
notes: Chain: Mack's post on X, reported by Futurism, relayed by dev.ua. Futurism's article not read. Account is Mack's own and some readers doubt it; score lowered by 1.
